newsitem.title: INDIA: India unit of U.S.computer firm NCR targets banks.
newsitem.headline: India unit of U.S.computer firm NCR targets banks.

text.p: Computer firm NCR Corp of the U.S. on Tuesday launched NCR Corp India Pvt Ltd, a fully-owned Indian subsidiary, to seize opportunities created by the rapid modernisation of India's far-flung network of banks, company officials said.

"India is one of the six largest emerging and strategic countries identified by NCR," said Victor Ang, NCR managing director for southeast Asia. "NCR is ready to invest in India to leverage the tremendous growth opportunities."

NCR has operated in India since 1994 as a unit of AT&T Global Information Solutions. It draws the bulk of its clients from the financial services sector, providing services to ten multinational private and public sector banks.
"Banking is easily more than half of our business and is likely to remain so," Ang said. "It's our core business."
He said NCR perceived an important role for itself as India's large public sector banks modernised to meet the demands of the country's five-year-old economic reforms programme.
"Even public sector banks have to start becoming competitive," Ang said.

"Many have been privatised, many are going to be floated soon. They will need to emphasise their individual identities, their different policies. They will have to differentiate themselves from each other. We are ready to help them."
India's 90 banks have, among them, a widespread network of 62,849 branches, the Reserve Bank of India says.
"There's now a major drive to be customer-sensitive in Indian banking," said K. Sambasivan, NCR's general manager in charge of sales and marketing.
"Only an insignificant portion have computerised. The opportunities are mind-boggling -- home banking, Internet banking..."

NCR India already has on hand orders for more than 50 automated teller machines (ATMs), officials said. It is in talks with numerous banks to provide circuitry for flexible "anytime, anywhere" banking as well as for cheque clearing centres.

Formerly AT&T Global Information Solutions, NCR Corp is to be spun off from U.S. telecommunications major AT&T as an independent publicly-traded $7-billion firm by the end of 1996, company officials said.
Ang said NCR intended to utilise Indian software expertise to generate packages for its parent company abroad.
"We have software development centres in Madras, Bangalore and Bombay," Ang said.
He said the upcoming divestiture from AT&T prevented him from providing financial details of NCR's operations in India.
"But we plan to double our growth every year for the next three years," he said.
